questions.q: How does a tensor core differ from a CUDA core?
options: A tensor core performs one multiply-accumulate per cycle, same as a CUDA core
A tensor core computes an entire small matrix multiply-accumulate as a single hardware operation
A tensor core is used only for memory transfers
A tensor core can only process integer data
questions.explain: A tensor core performs an entire small matrix multiply-accumulate operation in a single hardware step, rather than one scalar multiply-accumulate at a time like a CUDA core.

questions.q: Which precision format keeps FP32's exponent range but uses fewer mantissa bits?
options: FP16
BF16
INT8
FP64
questions.explain: BF16 (brain float 16) preserves FP32's exponent range, making it less prone to overflow than FP16, while using fewer mantissa bits for precision.

questions.q: What is the purpose of torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler in a mixed-precision training loop?
options: It converts the entire model to INT8 for inference
It scales the loss up before backward() to prevent small FP16 gradients from underflowing to zero, then unscales before the optimizer step
It permanently changes the model's weights to FP16
It disables tensor cores during training
questions.explain: GradScaler scales the loss value up so that small gradient values don't underflow to zero in FP16 during backpropagation, then unscales them before the optimizer applies the update.

questions.q: What does torch.autocast do in a training loop?
options: It automatically casts eligible operations like matrix multiplies to a lower precision while keeping numerically sensitive ones in FP32
It moves tensors from CPU to GPU
It disables all GPU memory allocation
It permanently converts the model to BF16
questions.explain: torch.autocast is a context manager that automatically runs eligible operations (like matmuls and convolutions) in a lower precision format while leaving numerically sensitive operations in FP32.

questions.q: What is TF32, and when does PyTorch use it?
options: A file format for storing trained models
A tensor-core-only internal format that PyTorch can use automatically for FP32 matrix multiplications on Ampere-or-newer GPUs
A compression algorithm for GPU memory
A deprecated format no longer supported by NVIDIA
questions.explain: TF32 is a tensor-core-only format with reduced mantissa precision that PyTorch can automatically substitute for ordinary FP32 matrix multiplications on Ampere-and-newer GPUs, trading a bit of precision for a large speedup.
